# Cartridge bus

One card edge joins a [Cartridge](glossary.md#term-cartridge) to the [Base unit](glossary.md#term-base-unit). The cartridge has gold fingers on its front edge. The base has a right-angle socket under the console, Samtec PCIE-164-02-F-D-RA.

The contact-by-contact table is `spec/generated/bus.md`, generated from `spec/ramspec.py`.

> [!CAUTION]
> **Mechanical fit only**
>
> The socket is the PCI Express x16 part. The pin assignment is this project's own. Never put a cartridge in a PC, and never put a PCI Express card in the tester.

## Contacts

| Group | Count | Level |
| --- | --- | --- |
| FPGA lines | 116 | 3.3 V. They do not tolerate 5 V |
| Ground | 24 | One ground position per six signal positions |
| DUT rail, [VDUT](glossary.md#term-vdut) | 8 | 2.5 V to 5.8 V |
| 3.3 V | 2 | Fixed rail |
| 5 V | 2 | Fixed rail |
| I2C | 4 | Two buses: cartridge ID (`ID_SDA`, `ID_SCL`) and SPD (`SPD_SDA`, `SPD_SCL`) |
| Sideband | 8 | `STRAP_5V_OK`, `ADP_PRESENT_N`, `DUT_PG`, `VDUT_SENSE`, `SPD_WP`, `AUX_EN`, `AUX_OK`, `ADP_INT_N` |

The groups add up to 164 contacts. Each FPGA line has a 22 ohm series resistor on the base board.

## Mechanical

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Cartridge board | 150 x 100 mm, 1.6 mm thick |
| Tongue | 84.3 x 8.4 mm, 20 degree bevel, key notch between positions 11 and 12 |
| Height above the base board | 5 mm to the underside of the cartridge board |
| Tallest part under the cartridge shell | 2.2 mm |
| Insertion | From the rear, on two rails |

The socket is rated for tens to low hundreds of insertions. Treat it as a wear part.

## Rules for a cartridge

1. Connect a socket pin to a bus signal contact only through a buffer. `check_buffered` in the board build fails otherwise.
2. Ground `STRAP_5V_OK` if the cartridge needs more than 3.8 V on VDUT. With the contact open, the base cuts the DUT switch above 3.85 V.
3. Expect every line to be high impedance while `DUT_PG` is low.

## Room for SDRAM

A 168-pin SDRAM DIMM needs 109 signals, so 116 lines leave room for that cartridge without a new base. The ground count is modest for 133 MHz. Check the signal integrity of that cartridge on the bench.
